title: JASMINE: Arabic GPT Models for Few-Shot Learning

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting the model with occupation templates (e.g., 'The <occupation> is often practiced by ...') and analyzing the linguistic gender of the autocompletions to measure occupational stereotypes. It is also measured via intersectional prompts combining gender, color, and region.

Prompting the model with combinations of color, gender, and region (e.g., 'You always find black American men working as ...'), and manually classifying the generated professions into high-wage, medium-wage, and low-wage categories.
Using intersectional prompt templates containing specific regions (Africa, Asia, America, Europe) and analyzing the socioeconomic status (wage levels) of the professions generated by the model.

Prompting the model with specific religious or ideological group names (e.g., Atheists, Islam, Judaism, Sunni, Shi'a) and evaluating the completions for abusive, dangerous, hateful, or offensive language using four SoTA classifiers.
